ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation and continuously thereafter, identify and screen all direct and indirect shareholders, UBOs, directors, senior managers, authorized signatories, introducers, material counterparties and relevant clients against United Nations sanctions lists, European Union restrictive-measures lists, Spanish national sanctions and terrorist lists, and OFAC lists as an additional risk-control measure where a United States nexus exists. Determine PEP, family-member and close-associate status under Law 10/2010 and apply enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification and enhanced transaction monitoring. A sanctions or adverse-media hit must be dispositioned through documented independent verification; confirmed matches require rejection, freezing or reporting as legally applicable. A securities broker must maintain risk-based customer due diligence, ongoing monitoring, suspicious-transaction reporting to SEPBLAC, record retention and internal-control procedures. OFAC is not generally the governing Spanish sanctions authority but can create material correspondent-banking and extraterritorial exposure.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), official electronic services portal: https://www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be distinct from existing registered names and comply with the Spanish Companies Act and Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Commercial Registry Regulation. The name may use Spanish or another legally acceptable language, but must be capable of registration and must not mislead as to the company's legal form, activity, public status or regulatory authorization. The legal-form designation 'Sociedad Limitada', 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or the permitted abbreviation 'S.L.' or 'S.R.L.' must be included. Foreign-language names and transliterations are subject to registrability, distinctiveness, public-order and non-confusion review. A name clearance does not authorize regulated investment services or imply CNMV authorization.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Submit an electronic or paper application to the Registro Mercantil Central identifying up to five proposed names in priority order and the applicant. If issued, the certificate reserves the name for six months from issuance for registration purposes; the certificate itself is generally usable for execution of the incorporation deed for three months, after which a new certificate may be required. If rejected, review the stated reason, eliminate phonetic or conceptual conflict, remove regulated or public-authority terminology, and submit a new prioritized application. A substantive challenge may be directed to the competent Commercial Registry authority and, where applicable, pursued through the administrative and judicial remedies available under the Commercial Registry Regulation and Spanish administrative-procedure law. Name acceptance does not replace CNMV authorization, trade-mark clearance, domain-name clearance or competition-law review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Spanish SL must have a registered office in Spain under the Companies Act. A serviced or virtual office may satisfy the formal registered-office requirement only where it provides a genuine address capable of receiving official notices and maintaining corporate records. It is not adequate as the sole operational base for a regulated retail securities broker. A CNMV authorization file should demonstrate appropriate premises, information-security controls, compliance and risk personnel, governance, books and records, client-asset controls, complaint handling, operational resilience and effective management in Spain or another permitted EEA location. A mailbox-only arrangement creates a high authorization, banking, AML and tax-substance risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No statutory probability is published. The risk is high for a proposed investment-services company: CNMV may request documentary evidence, conduct supervisory interviews and perform on-site inspections under its supervisory powers, and SEPBLAC or other competent authorities may inspect AML controls. For planning purposes only, an internal risk assumption of 50% to 75% inspection or substantive premises-verification exposure during authorization or early supervision is reasonable; this is not an official government probability.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), Articles 20–30, 58, 62–63, 175 and 209–211; Reglamento del Registro Mercantil (Royal Decree 1784/1996) Articles 120–135.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial for statutory inscription; Registro Mercantil Central for the corporate name certificate; Spanish Notary for the execution of the public deed.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución de Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (public incorporation deed), to be filed with the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 3,000 statutory minimum, fully subscribed and paid in cash at formation; funds must be deposited in an account opened in the name of the company in formation and evidenced by a bank certificate under Article 62 LSC; the deposited capital remains blocked until registration in the Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST CORPORATE RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY] SOCIEDAD DE RESPONSABILIDAD LIMITADA At a lawful meeting held at the registered office on [date], the founding members resolved unanimously as follows: 1. That the 1,000 shares comprising the share capital, each of a nominal value of EUR 3.00, are hereby subscribed and are fully paid by cash contribution, as evidenced by the bank deposit certificate issued by [bank] pursuant to Article 62 LSC. 2. That the company's registered office is fixed at [address], Madrid, Spain. 3. That [name of manager] is appointed as Administrador Único, with power to execute the public deed, obtain tax identification numbers, open bank accounts, and complete all registration filings. Approved by unanimous vote and signed on [date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Negative Certificate of Corporate Name
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a telematic request using a recognized Spanish digital certificate, or attend with a public representative, applying for a negative certification of the proposed Spanish SL name. Provide up to two alternative names in order of priority. The registry issues a certificate confirming that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered company. The certificate is valid for three months and must be used within that period.
required_dossiers: Passport or NIE of the founding members
Form of representative authority if filed by proxy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry objects because the proposed name coincides with an existing one, submit an alternative name without delay; a corrected request can be refiled electronically within one to two business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution or bank branch in Spain
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional bank account in the name of the company in formation, deposit at least EUR 3,000 from a founding member's personal account, and request a certificate showing the account title, IBAN and exact balance. The certificate must be dated not earlier than two months before the deed and must expressly identify the account holder as the Spanish SL in formation. The funds remain unavailable until the Mercantile Registry registers the company.
required_dossiers: Passports or NIE/TIE cards of all founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide any additional KYC or UBO documentation requested by the bank within 24 to 48 hours; if the name certificate expires while the account is being opened, obtain a renewed name certificate before finalizing the deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Notary (Notario) in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders and the appointed administrator appear before the notary with the negative name certificate, the bank deposit certificate, the approved articles of association and valid personal identification. The notary reviews the capacity and legality of the deed, records the subscribers' share allocations, incorporates the statutory clauses, reads the deed aloud and receives the administrator's acceptance. The notary then issues an authorized first copy for registration.
required_dossiers: Passports or NIE/TIE cards of all subscribers
Identity details of the appointed administrator
Proof of provisional NIF application if available
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires correction or missing documentation, remedy the defect and either re-execute the deed or formalize a supplementary public act before the same notary; the notary will provide guidance on any formal legal objection within the deed itself.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Capital-Operations Tax and Submission of Form 600
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oficina Liquidadora of the Consejería de Hacienda of the relevant Autonomous Community (e.g., Hacienda de la Comunidad de Madrid)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty business days after the execution of the deed, file Form 600 for the Impuesto sobre Transmisiones Patrimoniales y Actos Jurídicos Documentados, modalidad Operaciones Societarias, at the competent regional tax office. Attach the first copy of the public deed and compute the tax at the statutory rate on the nominal share capital. Obtain the stamped payment certificate which must be presented to the Mercantile Registry together with the deed.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office raises a query, file a corrective Form 600 and pay the stated adjustment within the granted term; if the taxable base is disputed, submit a written explanation and supporting statutory references, or lodge an appeal within thirty days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the deed is executed, apply for the provisional NIF (CIF) using Form 036 through the AEAT office corresponding to the registered office. Attach a notarized copy of the deed and evidence of the appointment of the administrator. The AEAT issues the provisional NIF which remains valid only until the company is registered; the definitive NIF is issued after registration.
required_dossiers: First copy or certified copy of the public deed
Passport or NIE of the appointed administrator
Minutes or document evidencing appointment of the administrator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEAT rejects or queries the application due to name or address discrepancies, correct Form 036 and resubmit; if the representative lacks a Spanish NIE, obtain the NIE before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription in the Registro Mercantil Provincial
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial first copy together with the stamped Form 600 and provisional NIF to the provincial Mercantile Registry. The registrar performs the statutory legal review (calificación) and, if satisfied, records the company, its share capital, corporate purpose, registered office and governing body. Construction of the statutory books and formal continuity of the entity commence after registration; the bank deposit can then be freely deployed.
required_dossiers: First copy of the public deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar suspends the entry on legal grounds, comply by executing a rectification deed before the original notary or by answering the registrar's note; resubmit within the term set out in the note, usually fifteen business days, or appeal the final decision to the Juzgado de lo Mercantil or the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive NIF, Legalization of Books and Governance Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Registro Mercantil Provincial
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Mercantile Registry issues the certificate of registration, submit Form 036 to convert the provisional NIF to the definitive NIF. Prepare corporate books in Spanish, including the libro de actas, libro de socios and libro de registro de acciones nominativas, and present them to the provincial Mercantile Registry for legalization. Record the appointment of the governing body in the registry and commence tax, accounting and corporate governance obligations effective from the deed date.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration issued by the Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry refuses legalization due to book format or pagination errors, rebind and resubmit within the applicable period; if the AEAT rejects the NIF conversion, file a correcting census declaration with the registration certificate as supporting evidence.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) for the regulated securities services activity; municipal authority (Ayuntamiento) for the physical establishment and activity license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorización para operar como Empresa de Servicios de Inversión (Agencia de Valores or Sociedad de Valores) under Ley 6/2023, de 17 de marzo, de los Mercados de Valores y de los Servicios de Inversión; plus municipal licencia de actividad / declaración responsable de apertura for office premises.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Consejería competente en materia de medio ambiente de la Comunidad Autónoma, coordinated at state level with the Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full Environmental Impact Assessment; office-based securities brokerage is not listed in Annex I or II of Ley 21/2013, de Evaluación Ambiental. Only a municipal environmental activity communication (memoria de actividad) may be required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, VOCs, combustion emissions or hazardous waste generation attributable to the brokerage activity; office wastewater discharge to the public sewer must meet the municipal non-domestic discharge limits; waste segregation and recycling obligations apply under Ley 7/2022; HVAC equipment must comply with EU F-Gas Regulation (EC) 517/2014.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal activity license or declaración responsable; fire safety certification under the CTE-DB-SI and Royal Decree 513/2017 (Regulamento de Instalaciones de Protección Contra Incendios); structural load inspection certificate for the occupied floors; workplace risk assessment and occupational health and safety compliance under Ley 31/1995 and Royal Decree 486/1997; emergency and evacuation plan; accessibility certificate; and, where legally required, registration of the workers' prevention service.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Non-resident Spanish SL entities obtain statutory NIF through AEAT online registration or in-person submission at tax offices, including incorporation deed, proof of address, and business activity documentation; processing requires 10-15 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch rules under EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive apply, with limited territorial scope options for specific offshore activities.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €30,000 annual taxable turnover triggering mandatory registration for non-agricultural activities
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time SII electronic invoicing with digital stamps for VAT-registered taxpayers exceeding €3 million turnover or in designated sectors; immediate API reporting to AEAT required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to exports of goods outside the EU or offshore services provided to non-EU clients where performance occurs outside Spain and no Spanish VAT nexus exists; for offshore securities brokerage, proof of non-EU client and offshore execution is mandatory.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Fraudulent zero-rating claims incur penalties up to 100% of evaded VAT, interest surcharges, and potential criminal prosecution; retrospective clawback of zero-rated amounts with loss of refund rights.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting as the central bank and national competent authority for monetary policy and financial stability; the Dirección General de Transacciones Internacionales (DGTI) under the Ministerio de Economía, Comercio y Empresa handles exchange control declarations and balance-of-payments reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible. Spain, as a eurozone member, maintains complete capital account liberalisation, permitting unrestricted conversion of capital and current account transactions, including for non-resident investors. Profit remittance is freely permitted for SL entities subject to standard corporate taxation, dividend withholding tax under Article 21 of the domestic Income Tax Act (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) when applicable, and applicable tax treaty rates. No prior exchange control approval is required for remittances exceeding thresholds; however, all cross-border flows must be declared to the Bank of Spain for statistical and balance-of-payments purposes (Circular 4/2012, updated by Circular 3/2017 and related regulations).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain does not impose mandatory surrender or conversion requirements on export proceeds. Companies may retain earnings in foreign currency or convert freely, subject only to anti-money-laundering and tax reporting obligations. Payment terms and invoice settlement are regulated under Spanish and EU commercial law; no statutory timeline exists for converting export receipts, although all cross-border payments above €10,000 must be reported to the Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Segregated Client Account as required for securities brokerage)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account (IBAN-ES segregated account)
Operational Account (IBAN-ES current account) / Settlement Account
Capital Escrow Account (for regulatory capital deposit) and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for primary treasury operations. Spanish and EU regulation require the securities brokerage to maintain client money in credit institutions or qualifying banks under Article 1 of Royal Decree-Law 21/2017 and MiFID II delegation requirements. Offshorer digital EMIs (e.g., UK, Baltic, or Singapore-licensed) cannot hold Spanish client funds as core clearing rails without an EU passport and must not serve as the principal segregated funds depository. They may be used only for ancillary operational payments, subject to strict AML review and Bank of Spain classification as electronic money institutions under Royal Decree 778/2023, provided they hold a valid EEA authorisation and pass enhanced due diligence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish banks generally require physical appearance of all directors, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) for onboarding of non-resident corporate entities, although some tier-1 banks allow hybrid video-identification if the corporate entity already has a Spanish tax residence certificate and a Spanish registered office. Under the Law 10/2010 on Prevention of Money Laundering, in-person identity verification or an equivalent high-assurance electronic identification (recognised EU qualified signature) is mandatory. A supervised face-to-face interview with the Compliance Officer or Director of the International Desk is normally compulsory when the commercial profile is a high-risk securities broker; remote opening for such high-risk categories is generally rejected unless a prior banking relationship or a designated Spanish agent is appointed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO ownership layer involving trusts or foundations in non-EU low-tax jurisdictions triggering enhanced due diligence (EDD) under Law 10/2010, Article 11
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of trust deeds, foundation statutes, commercial register extracts reflecting the full ownership chain, tax residence certificates for each intermediary entity, sworn declarations from directors providing source-of-wealth narrative, and a notarised organisational chart (Spanish or apostilled).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business scope: securities brokerage / CFD retail distribution activates the high-risk professional category requiring additional information on transaction profile, target clients, and segregation mechanisms.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licence from the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores (CNMV) or proof that the entity is a tied agent of an EU-licensed investment firm; robust AML/CFT manual (Spanish version); business continuity policy; client onboarding procedures; annual audited financial statements; and bank reference letters from the parent bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high transaction volume through Visa/Mastercard rails and cross-border wire transfers triggering automated transaction-monitoring flagging (SEPBLAC thresholds and unusual activity patterns)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed product and service prospectus with risk class limits, payment routing schema, segregation ledger software description, independent auditor opinion on internal capital adequacy, and a firm commitment to submit monthly STR/SAR reports with an independent compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director residing outside the EU without a Spanish tax ID (NIF) causing identity and tax residency confusion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies, original or apostilled NIE/NIF references, proof of a physical Spanish address or appointment of a Spanish fiscal representative, original D-2311 and D-2325 forms filed with the Spanish tax agency, and a signed declaration of the absence of any offshore shell company purpose.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Injection of initial share capital and subordinated loans must be executed via SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's bank to the Spanish SL's operational euro account (IBAN ES91...). For capital increases, the remitter must use CFDI code 8000 (transfers of capital) or equivalent under Bank of Spain Circular 4/2012; the recipient bank must receive the original capital contribution deed and notarised resolution. For capital exceeding €3,000,000, a prior bank AML clearance and a written source-of-funds substantiation (audited financial statements, tax returns, or sale contracts) will be required. All inbound funds should be labelled 'CAPITAL INJECTION – SHARE PREMIUM – NO INVOICE' with the company's CIF/NIF in the reference field to avoid misclassification as commercial income.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlement disbursements for retail securities brokerage operations are executed through SWIFT MT103 on the domestic SEPA rail for euro-denominated transfers, and SWIFT MT103 on the correspondent banking network for non-EUR currencies. For commercial trade flows (if the brokerage expands into custody or corporate finance ancillary services) the primary rail is the documentary Letter of Credit (LC) with SWIFT MT700/MT707 series, together with the standard ICC UCP 600 rules. All outbound payments must include the required end-use declaration code and be reconciled against contract reference numbers. For client withdrawals from segregated wallets, payments must be initiated only to the client's own verified bank account on file to satisfy CNMV client-asset protection rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency Forwards (plain vanilla OTC EUR/foreign currency) executed with an EU-authorised credit institution under MiFID II — permitted for hedging net exposure from securities settlement and client funding.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in non-convertible or restricted currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Venezuelan bolívar) where the Spanish brokerage has Latin American client settlement exposure; permitted only as risk-management instruments, not speculative.
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) between EUR and USD/GBP/CHF for matching long-term asset and liability streams of the treasury pool.
FX options (call/put) used solely for mitigation of market risk arising from the brokerage's proprietary positions, subject to internal risk limits and Bank of Spain financial reporting.
